source.title: Representation Transitions Reveal Emerging Safety Risks in Multi-Turn LLM Agents
source.authors: Hao-Yu Wang; Wei Zhao; Ye-Di Zhang; Christopher M. Poskitt; Jun Sun

record.file_problem: None apparent; the provided paper text includes the main text and appendices through the monitoring-overhead section.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses contrastive representation directions as a tool for detecting and intervening on agent risks, but does not test whether the refusal direction mediates refusal to users. Its direction, target behavior, and interventions differ from the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the original refusal-direction work as background and develops a different transition-space direction for detecting injected instructions and multi-turn agent risks. Those agent-behavior and direction-steering results do not measure refusal toward users, or whether the claimed refusal direction preserves general capability. DART’s benchmark results and reminder-induced refusals are therefore not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study builds its own harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means direction over last-token representation transitions in agent trajectories. It uses that direction to detect injected instructions and multi-turn decomposition attacks. It cites Arditi et al. only as background. It never extracts, ablates or adds the refusal direction, and never measures refusal to users as a function of that direction. The direct-steering results (Appendix F.3) suppress injected agent actions along the study's own injection direction, which is a different construct. The refusals it reports come from a prompted reminder that says 'say you cannot help', so refusal is induced on purpose. Classing this as T4 rather than T6 is borderline: the study reuses the contrastive difference-in-means technique, not the refusal direction itself.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase reflects only the Appendix F findings. The paper's main conclusion is different: DART, a monitor over denoised representation transitions, detects multi-turn agent attacks, attributes them to a context segment, and mitigates them with reminders. It cuts ASR from 84% to 25% on MT-AgentRisk and from 97% to 52% on ASEval at low utility cost. Denoising is critical for sparse attacks. The appendix adds that the direction is mainly structural and that direct steering works only in a narrow window. The paper draws no conclusion about the refusal-direction claim.
record.recipe_differences: The study forms a contrastive direction from harmful and benign representation transitions at a selected layer, denoises it for trajectory monitoring, and tests targeted agent interventions. It does not use the original difference of mean harmful and harmless instruction activations to ablate refusal across every layer and position or to add refusal-inducing direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Direct steering results vary strongly with layer depth and steering strength; the reported effect concentrates in the frac 0.35–0.65 band at α=2 and is weak outside it. The monitor’s denoising and detection performance also depends on benchmark and direction construction, but those results do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: The study's difference-in-means transition direction flags benign injected imperatives (98%) nearly as often as malicious ones (100%). It does not flag long benign narratives (0%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A contrastive harmful-minus-benign direction fit on agent injections primarily encodes injected-instruction structure rather than harmfulness.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a fixed wrapper, the direction still separates malicious from benign goals (mean 0.97; 0.89 against action-matched benign goals). It transfers to an unseen injection phrasing at 0.96 accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agent-injection directions carry a weaker but real harm-correlated component and generalize across attack phrasings.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual-stream steering toward the clean-mean projection suppresses injected agent actions only at mid layers with α=2 (0.43 in the band vs 0.05 outside; peak 0.68). Late-layer steering fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering along an agent-risk reading direction has causal effect on injected actions only in a narrow layer and strength window.

record.problems: The direct-steering effect is localized to a hand-tuned layer and strength, which the authors say lack a calibration procedure. The larger replication reports 37 Qwen3-14B cases; the paper describes a narrow steering window and weak effects outside it. These results concern agent actions, not refusal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Main benchmark detection and mitigation results concern agent trajectory risk and reminders, rather than the claimed refusal direction or user-facing refusal behavior.

untested.parts: Refusal direction extraction, ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal, capability preservation.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction; adversarial training against ablation.
Multi-dimensional or affine accounts of refusal.
Separation of harmfulness encoding from refusal. The F.2 finding that the direction is structural with a weaker harm component concerns the study's injection direction, not refusal.
Transfer of the refusal direction across languages, variants, or from base to instruct models.
Training dependence of a removable refusal direction.
Refusal direction in reasoning models. Qwen3 models are used, but refusal mediation is not studied.

record.verdict_notes: None of the rows bear on any version. The reminder-induced refusals and the soft-suffix optimization toward a refusal continuation are deliberate inductions, not measurements of a refusal direction. The study also has a borderline case for cites_only/T6, since its only link to the claim is a citation and a shared difference-in-means technique.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the claimed refusal direction, refusal removal or induction, or preservation of other abilities after ablating it.
No weight edit removing the refusal direction in released models.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Does not compare affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal.
Does not test whether a model’s harmfulness judgment is separately encoded from its refusal decision.
Does not test transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary refusal training to test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
Does not test reasoning models’ refusal direction.

rows.check: The subject is mislabeled. The 48/111 figure pools 111 complying trajectories from Qwen3-14B, Qwen3-32B and Qwen3-30B-A3B. The text also describes the replication as 37 Qwen3-14B cases, so the subject should be a pooled set, not Qwen3-14B alone. The measure is suppression of injected actions, not refusal, so 'partial' against a claim version is not meaningful.
